sentences.text: Revenue moved from $41.9 billion in FY2016 to $47.9 billion in FY2025, a 1.5% CAGR [F1][F10][F219].
The path was a refranchising-driven step down, not compounding: revenue fell 13.5% in FY2017 and 5.3% in FY2018 before recovering [D42][D93].
Bottling Investments revenue fell 42.8% in FY2017 and 40.0% in FY2018 as bottling territories were refranchised [D572][D575][P71].
Operating margin then stepped up from 20.7% in FY2016 to 26.7% in FY2018, and FY2025 set a window high of 28.7% [F41][F43][F50][D765].
The FY2025 jump of 7.5pp came mainly from lower other operating charges after the prior-year fairlife contingent-consideration remeasurement [D463][P12].
Concentrate operations supplied 59.4% of FY2025 revenue and 1.6pp of the 1.9% growth [D532][D534][D449].
Finished product operations in the US added 1.3pp, while non-US finished product operations subtracted 1.0pp [D562][D555].
Worldwide concentrate sales volume grew 1% in FY2025, with EMEA up 3% and Latin America even [P16][P19][P18].
Operating income grew 37.7% against 1.9% revenue growth, an incremental margin of 428.4% [D450][D449][D473].
Diluted EPS grew 23.6% against 23.3% net income growth, with the diluted share count down 0.2% [D453][D451][D468].
Operating margin of 28.7% in FY2025 sits above the 26.0% window median and at the window high [F50][D766][D765].
Gross margin of 61.6% is 0.9pp above its 60.7% median, with cost of revenue at 38.4% of revenue [F30][D772][D428].
The FY2025 gross margin gain of 0.6pp came from pricing and prior-year refranchising, partly offset by currency and commodities [D462][P14].
SG&A fell 0.4% and added 0.7pp to margin on lower Foundation contributions and incentive expense [D466][D476][P13].
Net margin of 27.3% nearly matched operating margin, helped by a 17.9% effective tax rate and $1.1 billion of other income [F70][D435][X100].
Free cash flow of $5.3 billion was 0.40x net income in FY2025, the window low against a 0.97x median [F120][F60][D437][D778].
Operating cash flow rose 8.9% on strong cash operating results and lower tax payments [D454][P1].
Capex of $2.1 billion was 4.4% of revenue and 2.01x D&A, the highest multiple in the window [F110][D432][D438].
The FY2024 collapse in conversion followed a $6.0 billion IRS tax litigation deposit [D404][P22].
Net cash was $8.8 billion at FY2025, or 18.3% of revenue, against $10.3 billion of cash and investments [D442][D443][D440].
That ranks at the 100th percentile of six staples peers, whose median net cash is -14.5% of revenue [D793][D794].
Buybacks plus dividends of $9.5 billion were 179.9% of free cash flow, funded partly by $5.0 billion of debt issued [D444][D445][X155].
Return on average equity was 46.0%, above the 36.5% peer median [D448][D798].
FY2017 and FY2018 revenue in the table are later recasts: $36.2 billion versus $35.4 billion first reported, and $34.3 billion versus $31.9 billion [F2][X2][F3][X3].
Growth and margins spanning those years mix two presentations, so the FY2017-FY2018 comparisons are unreliable [R1].
Payouts exceeded free cash flow in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, reaching 214.2% in FY2024 [D344][D395][D445].
Free cash flow stayed below 80% of net income in FY2024 and FY2025, at 0.45x and 0.40x [D387][D437].
Total debt rose 31.3% in FY2025 to $1.5 billion, though the level remains small against cash [D470][D441][D440].
Free cash flow to net income: a move back toward the 0.97x window median would confirm the cash recovery; another year near 0.40x would extend the weak conversion [D778][D437].
Operating margin: holding above the 26.0% median would confirm the FY2025 step-up; a fall back toward the 21.2% FY2024 level would reverse it [D766][F49].
Buybacks plus dividends against free cash flow: a ratio below the 179.9% FY2025 level would ease the funding gap; above it would widen reliance on debt [D445].
